meta.name: ReliefMap Knowledge Base
meta.description: Local disaster-relief knowledge base used by ReliefBot AI when the backend/OpenAI is unavailable.

intents.answer: ReliefMap is an AI-powered community disaster relief coordination platform. It helps citizens, NGOs, and volunteers monitor disasters, coordinate relief efforts, manage shelters and food centers, track hospitals, and access live emergency information — all in real time.

ReliefMap works in 4 steps:
1. Citizens & authorities report disasters (floods, fires, cyclones, earthquakes) via the 'Report a Disaster' form.
2. The AI analyzes each report and assigns a risk score and severity level.
3. Relief centers, volunteers, and NGOs are automatically mobilized and resources are allocated.
4. Everyone tracks live updates on the map, analytics, and news feed.

Here's how to find the nearest shelter:
• Open the Live Map and enable the 'Shelters' filter.
• Shelters show capacity and available facilities.
• During an emergency, AI prioritizes the nearest open shelter with the most space.

You can also ask me for a specific location and I'll point you to the closest option.

Food distribution centers are operating across the region. To find the nearest one:
• Open the Live Map and filter by 'Food Centers'.
• Each center shows available quantity and distance.

If you need immediate food relief, head to the closest open Food Center or contact the coordination team.

To find nearby hospitals and medical help:
• Open the Live Map and filter by 'Hospitals'.
• Each hospital shows emergency availability and bed status.

For life-threatening medical emergencies, call 112 immediately.

NGOs are a key part of ReliefMap. They manage relief operations, coordinate missions, and distribute resources. You can:
• Register as an NGO to manage operations.
• Partner with us through the Contact page.
• View NGO-coordinated missions on the dashboard.

Volunteering is easy! Here's what to do:
1. Register/log in and select the 'Volunteer' role.
2. View available missions on your dashboard.
3. Accept missions and get deployed to disaster zones.

Requirements: valid ID, willingness to help, and basic emergency training (provided by ReliefMap).

Thank you for wanting to help! You can donate:
• Food — drop off at any Food Center or shelter.
• Medicine — to hospitals and medical stations.
• Money — via the coordination team.
• Clothes — at designated collection points.

Every contribution is tracked and allocated where it's needed most.

Official Flood Safety Guidelines:
• Move to higher ground immediately.
• Avoid walking or driving through floodwater.
• Turn off electricity and gas before evacuating.
• Do not drink floodwater — it's contaminated.
• Keep an emergency kit with food, water, and medicine.
• Stay tuned to relief alerts and follow evacuation orders.

If you're trapped, call 112 or the emergency hotline.

Cyclone Safety Precautions:
• Stay indoors and away from windows.
• Secure loose objects that could become projectiles.
• Stock up on water, food, batteries, and a first-aid kit.
• Move to a designated shelter if ordered to evacuate.
• Avoid coastal areas and low-lying regions.
• Keep your phone charged and follow official alerts.

Earthquake Safety Tips:
• Drop, Cover, and Hold On.
• Stay away from windows, glass, and heavy furniture.
• If indoors, stay there — do not run outside.
• If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings.
• After shaking, expect aftershocks and check for injuries.
• Follow relief team instructions for evacuation.

Fire Safety Guidelines:
• If a fire starts, evacuate immediately and call 112.
• Stay low to avoid smoke inhalation.
• Feel doors before opening — if hot, find another exit.
• Never use water on electrical or oil fires.
• Have a fire extinguisher and know how to use it.
• Keep a meeting point outside your home.

Emergency Contacts:
• National Emergency Helpline: 112
• Ambulance: 108
• Fire: 101
• Police: 100
• Disaster Management: 1078
• ReliefMap Coordination Team: +91 96772 18987

Save these numbers and share them with your family.

Basic First Aid Tips:
• Call 112 immediately for emergencies.
• For bleeding, apply firm pressure with a clean cloth.
• For burns, cool with running water for 10 minutes.
• Do NOT move someone with a suspected spinal injury.
• If someone is unconscious but breathing, place them on their side.
• Perform CPR only if you are trained (30 compressions : 2 breaths).

Disaster Preparedness Checklist:
• Prepare an emergency kit: water, food, flashlight, batteries, first aid, medicines, important documents.
• Create a family emergency plan and meeting point.
• Know the nearest shelter and evacuation routes.
• Keep emergency contacts saved and written down.
• Stay informed via ReliefMap alerts.

Preparedness saves lives — start today!

Food availability is monitored in real time across all Food Centers. Open the Live Map and filter by 'Food Centers' to see current stock levels and quantities. You can also ask me about a specific center and I'll check its availability.

Medicine availability is tracked at hospitals and medical stations. Open the Live Map and filter by 'Hospitals' to view medical supply status. For urgent medication needs, contact the nearest hospital or the coordination team.

Clean drinking water is distributed at Food Centers and shelters. Open the Live Map and filter by 'Food Centers' to find water distribution points. Remember: never drink floodwater, as it is contaminated.

For navigation to relief centers, shelters, hospitals, and food points:
• Use the Live Map which pins all relief locations.
• Use the 'My Location' button to center the map on you.
• Enable the relevant filter to highlight what you need.

If you need directions to a specific place, tell me the place name and location, and I'll help.

Hello! I'm ReliefBot AI, your disaster relief assistant. I can help you find shelters, food, hospitals, volunteer opportunities, donation options, and share vital safety tips. What do you need help with today?
You're most welcome! Stay safe and don't hesitate to ask if you need anything else. ReliefMap is here for you. 🙏

I'm ReliefBot AI — the intelligent assistant of ReliefMap. I'm here to help citizens, NGOs, and volunteers during disasters by providing real-time relief information, safety guidelines, and coordination support.

The Live Map shows all relief centers, shelters, hospitals, food centers, and volunteer locations in real time. Just click the button below to open it. You can filter by category and use 'My Location' for navigation.

To donate:
• Money — contact the coordination team for bank details.
• Food — drop off at any Food Center.
• Medicine — deliver to the nearest hospital.
• Clothes — use designated collection points.

Every donation is logged and distributed to those in need. Contact us to coordinate your contribution.

To register on ReliefMap:
1. Click 'Login' on the top bar.
2. Switch to the 'Register' tab.
3. Choose your role: Citizen, NGO, or Volunteer.
4. Fill in your details and create your account.

Once registered, you can report disasters, volunteer, and access personalized relief tools.

To report a disaster:
1. Click 'Report a Disaster' on the dashboard.
2. Enter your name, contact, and location.
3. Select the disaster type and severity.
4. Describe the situation and submit.

The AI will analyze your report, assign a risk score, and alert the relief team for deployment.

The Analytics page shows:
• Relief center distribution
• Daily rescue trends
• Resource usage
• Volunteer allocation

This helps coordinators make data-driven decisions during disasters.
The News page provides real-time updates from disaster zones, relief operations, and priority alerts. You can search for specific news and read featured stories about ongoing relief efforts.

Your Profile page lets you manage your personal information, phone, email, and photo. You can also track your missions completed, volunteers led, field reports, and alerts. Go to Settings to customize your theme and language.
